key_insight: This study establishes the first U.S. CADASIL natural history cohort, providing a baseline benchmark for a monogenic small-vessel disease model of VCID.
clinical_relevance: The cohort’s standardized clinical, cognitive, imaging, and biomarker data can help improve trial readiness and comparisons for future VCID research.
method: Cross-sectional baseline analysis from a 12-site longitudinal cohort (Oct 2022–Jan 2025).
Recruited adults from families with documented NOTCH3 variants using clinical referrals, records, advocacy groups, and outreach.
Applied central genetic classification, standardized clinical assessments, MRI, and proteomics under harmonized protocols.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 560 baseline participants, with an analytic cohort of 343 CADASIL carriers and 116 non-carrier family controls, and uses group comparisons plus multivariable adjustment.
watch_item: Findings are baseline and largely cross-sectional, so they describe cohort characteristics rather than disease progression or causal effects.
paper_title: The United States CADASIL Consortium: Baseline Findings from a Natural History Study
